interpretation: Same fwp compiler, source, inputs, flags and memory mode with only numeric zip/map combination disabled/enabled. Other mapped-array/fold optimizations remain enabled. One warmup and eight alternating whole-process samples. Separate collection-disabled profiles prove counted cleanup. Retains and allocation requests are measured, not inferred from timings. No C/Rust comparison or universal speedup claim.
instructionScope: Actual native disassembly and generated code for selected direct ARC workload functions. Separate symbols may disappear through inlining. These are static function bodies, not total dynamic instruction counts or a register-spill classification. Linux ARM64 inlines vector fmul in the work loop; Linux AMD64 uses scalar mulsd with unrolling.

ubuntu-latest.head: 91146d684d723d835474e2a893a8adbe23004996

direct.source:
work : List[F64] -> List[F64]
work = both id (map (add 1.0)) | uncurry zip | map (uncurry mul)
main = range 0 128 | map (const (range 0 4096 | map int.to-float)) | map work | map sum | sum | echo

derivative.source: main = range 0 512 | map (const (range 0 4096 | map int.to-float) | vjp (map (mul 2.0)) (repeat 4096 1.0) | sum) | sum | echo

nested.source:
square : List[t] -> t where Ring[t], Dup[t]
square = head | option.unwrap-or zero | fork mul id id
main = range 0 256 | map int.to-float | grad (grad square | sum) | sum | echo
